author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Copper prices reached a record Tuesday as demand from AI data centers and other power-intensive industries met concerns about supply and possible tariffs.

Barron’s reported that New York front-month copper futures rose 2.8% to $6.78 per pound, surpassing the previous record. Mining shares also advanced as investors priced in the possibility of sustained demand.

Copper is a useful marker for the physical buildout behind digital services. Data centers, transmission upgrades and electric vehicles all require substantial amounts of the metal, even as miners face long development timelines.
The move is a reminder that the AI economy is not only a software story. Materials, electricity, construction and regional infrastructure are part of the same investment cycle.
dek: Demand from data centers, electrical grids and electric vehicles is colliding with supply constraints and trade-policy uncertainty.
headline: Record copper prices show the material cost of the AI boom
